newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels kill policeman, injure five.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels kill policeman, injure five.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas stormed two towns just south of Bogota, killing one policeman and wounding five others, officials said on Sunday.

The first assault took place on Saturday evening in Une, about 15 miles (25 km) outside the capital. One policeman was wounded as Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels attacked a police post.

Fighting broke out shortly afterwards in the town of Gutierrez, another 10 miles (15 km) south of Une, and lasted until the early hours of Sunday, said Gen. Alfredo Salgado, operational head of the National Police. One policeman died and four others were injured in the fight, he said.

FARC rebels, meanwhile, released two Brazilian highway engineers they kidnapped last August, a Red Cross official said. The two men were freed late on Friday near the city of Villavicencio, the capital of eastern Meta province.
Demetrio Mendoza and Eduardo Babtista had been supervising the building of a new highway between Bogota and Villavicencio, gateway to the eastern plains region.
Unconfirmed media reports suggested the men were handed over in exchange for a $1 million.

The FARC is Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army. It was set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964 and partly finances its long-running uprising with the proceeds of kidnappings and extortion.
